assets.name: salon-fireplace-limestone
assets.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: seamless physically based 3D base-color material. Input reference image is the photographed fireplace of La Bastide de Fléchon, reference only. Generate a NEW square 2048px texture scan of ONE CONTINUOUS pale creamy white limestone surface matching the fireplace lintel and hearth, about 80 cm square of stone. Near-smooth soft honed chalky ivory limestone, tiny scattered warm grey pores, minute warm beige mineral freckles, extremely subtle cloudy old patina, a few very faint hairline natural mineral marks. It is finely finished old limestone, NOT rough rubble, not crumbling, not concrete, not marble and not heavily speckled travertine. Do NOT draw joints, blocks, chips at edges, moldings or fireplace; editable geometry will provide those. Match pale cream body under neutral daylight with no orange firelight. Flat orthographic albedo, uniform neutral diffuse color, no baked shadows, no occlusion, no highlights or vignette, seamless all edges. Fill image only with material, no objects/text.
reference_photographs: PHOTOS/VICTOR FITZ/DSC05439-Edit-2.jpg
assets.output_edits: None. Exact generated PNG copied into project.
assets.limitations: Photo-informed visual interpretation, not measured reflectance or photogrammetry. Minor generated texture deviations remain; metric geometry and shader controls determine physical relief.

assets.name: salon-charred-oak-bark
assets.prompt: Use case: photorealistic-natural. Asset type: seamless PBR base-color texture for editable charred oak firewood logs in La Bastide de Fléchon's salon fireplace. Input images reference ONLY: look closely at the logs on the hearth in the supplied source fireplace. Generate NEW 2048px square orthographic material scan of a single continuous 45cm square oak BARK surface, natural broken split ridges running VERTICALLY bottom to top along the log, dark muted grey-brown furrows, pale ash-grey flaky char islands, remaining dark umber/tobacco wood fibres, thin irregular cracks across the long bark ribbons. Partially burned weathered oak, NOT smooth sawn timber, not a photograph of multiple logs, not uniform coal. The bark should have complex irregular overlapping grey-brown scales and lengthwise fibres at 5–30mm scale. Albedo color only: neutral flat uniform diffuse illumination, remove fire orange and all cast shadow or occlusion directionality. NO flames, embers, glow, smoke, room, ironwork, people or log silhouette/ends. No glossy burnt highlights, no vignette, no text. Texture fills frame edge-to-edge and is seamlessly tileable horizontally and vertically. Real substantial bark ridges will be provided in separate editable 3D geometry; do not depict scene lighting.

shader_policy.color: Images feed base color only through optional neutral saturation/gain calibration.
shader_policy.roughness: Material-specific ranges driven by an independent metric noise signal; no texture luminance input.
shader_policy.relief: Independent metric noise and crossing yarn signals. Major edges, joints, carved profiles, cushions and creases remain actual geometry.
shader_policy.reflectance: Principled physical IOR/Fresnel retained at specular IOR level 0.5. Stone/plaster/textile roughness and metal fractions vary by material. No global specular suppression.
shader_policy.scope: New salon_* material datablocks only; no shared house material mutation.
shader_policy.curtain: Diffuse + transmitted fiber mix, with small independent open-weave transparent fraction.
shader_policy.floor: Two separately generated stone albedos, each with a second subtle color calibration variant; normalized tile UVs receive deterministic object offsets. No image-painted tile grout.
shader_policy.rug: Single full-rug normalized UV. Simple espresso field, broad rust-red border, narrow dark binding. No invented ornamental carpet motifs.
shader_policy.upholstery: Sofa uses room-specific 25cm basketweave scan at 4 repeats/metre on physical-metre cloth UVs; large hemp pillows use physical UVs at 5.5 repeats/metre. Independent yarn normals follow those cloth UVs.
shader_policy.bark: Room-specific partially charred oak scan, normalized cylindrical side UVs U=circumference/V=length, scale U1/V2. Independent metric micro-normal and roughness; substantial bark ridges remain geometry.

material_calibration_passes.color_space_check: All albedo images are sRGB. Mean decoded linear RGB before gains: timber [.453,.352,.252], floor A [.692,.605,.484], floor B [.694,.615,.497]; no color-space bug found.

timber.reason: Reduce main-beam reflectance toward weathered grey-brown oak while retaining full generated grain and independent detail.

floor.reason: Small salon-only albedo calibration preserves pale warm beige and subtle four-material tile variations; no global exposure adjustment.

rubble.reason: Buff/grey limestone faces should be visibly darker than cream mortar, with natural block variation.

material_calibration_passes.verification: Beam/floor gains rendered in the saved draft house at frame385, Cycles24 samples, same camera and lighting; out/salon-study/timber-floor-adjusted.png. Rubble adjustment based on inspected neutral closeup and source31 without another simultaneous Blender worker.
material_calibration_passes.limitations: A photographic reflectance interpretation, not measured albedo. Bright aperture illumination still reduces floor contrast in the draft; source-linked lighting comparison remains necessary.

final_surface_calibration.method: Visual comparison of integrated Cycles previews with the unchanged originals; inferred reflectance, not measured BRDF.
final_surface_calibration.mortar_reason: The prior mortar was too white relative to stone in the frontal original, making every block look outlined. The final gain lowers that contrast independently of stone color.
final_surface_calibration.bark_reason: The isolated firebox render exposed overly pale bark under the modeled fire; pigment gain reduced while geometric splits and ash variation remain.
final_surface_calibration.rubble_geometry: Broader flatter faces, 16–25 mm projections, irregular perimeter points and 120–550 mm piece widths. Mortar is separate physical geometry.
final_surface_calibration.final_acceptance: See salon verification and exact rendered model hashes; these controls alone do not prove photographic identity.
